entrypoints.summary: A webpage invokes navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition with an attacker-supplied callback after the user grants that webpage Geolocation API permission.

affected_components.role: Injected Geolocation API spoofing logic; report says the callback is executed in hookedObj context that retains original API references.

code_slices.fixed: Exact patch code is not supplied. The report recommendation is to make original Geolocation API functions inaccessible to potentially malicious webpages.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The extension injects a script into all webpages that overrides Geolocation API methods to return VPN-location coordinates when spoofing is enabled.
code_slices.vulnerable: The report describes a wrapper that invokes a page-provided callback in `hookedObj` context; `hookedObj` retains original `getCurrentPosition` and `watchPosition` references.

negative_controls: Do not treat the behavior as permissionless: the report requires explicit webpage geolocation consent.
Without usable browser location signals, a real location may not be resolved.
observability.positive_marker: The PoC logs a fake position followed by a real position obtained through the original `getCurrentPosition` reference.

preconditions: The extension's Spoof your location feature is enabled.
The webpage obtains the user's explicit Geolocation API permission.
Browser location resolution yields real-location information; the report specifically discusses enabled WiFi and location services despite an active VPN.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A JavaScript callback supplied as the first argument to the hooked Geolocation API method; it relies on `this` being hookedObj.
trigger_steps.summary: Invoke navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition with a page-controlled callback that logs the spoofed result, invokes `this.getCurrentPosition(console.log)`, and sets `this.fakeGeo=false`.

impact.affected_asset: User real-world location, including location resolved by browser location services from IP and nearby wireless-access-point information.
impact.attacker_capability: A webpage that receives the user's explicit Geolocation API permission can recover and invoke the original location primitive through the callback receiver, and can disable fake-location handling for subsequent calls.
impact.security_effect: Conditional disclosure of the user's real geolocation, bypassing the extension's location-spoofing privacy feature.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker-controlled webpage supplies the callback passed to the extension-hooked getCurrentPosition function; the reported PoC does so from page JavaScript.

The injected spoofing wrapper executes that caller-supplied callback with hookedObj as its receiver/context, and hookedObj retains references to the original getCurrentPosition and watchPosition methods.
The callback calls this.getCurrentPosition(console.log), reaching the retained original API method; it can also set this.fakeGeo=false to disable hooked handling for later calls.

With explicit per-page geolocation consent, the page can observe real location instead of VPN-derived spoofed coordinates. The report states testing confirmed possible leakage on devices with enabled WiFi despite active VPN and enabled spoofing.

failure.operation: Invocation of the original Geolocation API through `this.getCurrentPosition(...)` from the attacker-supplied callback running with hookedObj context.

primary_invariant.kind: capability confinement across a callback boundary
primary_invariant.statement: Page-supplied callbacks invoked by the location-spoofing wrapper must not receive a receiver or reachable object that exposes the original browser Geolocation API methods.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The wrapper invokes the untrusted callback in hookedObj context, and hookedObj retains the original getCurrentPosition and watchPosition references.

raw_refs.role: canonical audit finding, PoC, affected-code excerpt, recommendation, and report-verified fix note

quality.review_notes: The primary public audit report supplies the finding narrative, affected-file/code-context excerpt, PoC, recommendation, and states Cure53 reviewed the related diff/PR and verified the issue no longer exists. The actual ExpressVPN patch/PR and a versioned vulnerable extension source snapshot are absent, so patch-level mechanics and exact affected release scope cannot be independently checked. Exploitation is conditional on feature enablement, explicit webpage geolocation consent, and available browser location signals; it is not permissionless disclosure.

remediation.invariant_restored: Original Geolocation API functions are inaccessible to potentially malicious webpages, including through the receiver/context used to invoke page-provided callbacks.
mitigation_classes: remove original API capability from untrusted callback context

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Version-specific vulnerable extension release/commit is not stated; report dated 2024-07-24 and published at Cure53 publications commit 3070b31cf51e966d504303936f0a12f20b198911.

target.component: Injected Geolocation API location-spoofing hook (reported affected file: xv_chrome/xv_chrome/source/scripts/content/gps.js)

oracle.expected_negative: When the original methods are inaccessible to the page callback, callback code cannot obtain a real position by invoking an original method through its receiver, and cannot use that receiver to disable fake-location handling.
oracle.expected_positive: Under the reported vulnerable behavior and after the user grants geolocation permission, the PoC first logs the spoofed position and then logs a real position via `this.getCurrentPosition(console.log)`; it also sets `this.fakeGeo=false`.
